articles.title: Cornell rape accuser faces threats demanding she drop her lawsuit, attorney says
articles.summary: The accuser’s attorney said that women mistakenly identified as Jane Doe have also received threats and that he received one Sunday morning.
articles.body:
The woman who alleges she was sexually assaulted by Cornell University fraternity members has received threats pressuring her to drop her lawsuit, her attorney said Sunday.

Thomas Giuffra told CNN's "State of the Union" that people attempting to unmask his client's identity had also targeted at least three women mistakenly identified as her. The former Cornell student is identified as Jane Doe in court documents.

"She's received multiple threats, and women who aren't even Jane Doe receive threats," Giuffra said. He added that he had received a threat Sunday morning.

Giuffra did not identify those responsible or say whether the threats had been reported to law enforcement. He did not immediately respond to NBC News' request for more information about the threats.

Jane Doe filed a lawsuit last month against Cornell and seven Chi Phi fraternity members, alleging she was sexually assaulted over the course of hours on Oct. 19-20, 2024, while she was under the influence of ketamine, alcohol and marijuana.

The allegations have sparked renewed scrutiny of the university's and local authorities' handling of the allegations. Gov. Kathy Hochul last week appointed New York Attorney General Letitia James as a special prosecutor to consider whether criminal charges are appropriate.

NBC News reported Friday that Cornell police interviewed witnesses and received anonymous tips during their investigation in 2024, but Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten did not review that additional information before deciding not to pursue charges at the time. He has defended his decision, saying that Jane Doe's initial six-page statement to police did not allege criminality.

Cornell President Michael Kotlikoff said Saturday that the university must do better and that its board of trustees would announce an independent review of its handling of the case next week.

articles.body: Jay Cinco and Lala Baptiste have ended their relationship months after getting engaged in March 2026. The two influencers announced their split in separate Instagram Stories on October 2, saying they had made the decision together and wanted to focus on themselves.Both made it clear that there was no bad blood between them. Cinco and Baptiste share a daughter and said they will continue to be there for her, meaning they will still spend time together as a family.Neither has given a specific reason for the breakup. He made clear that the end of their romantic relationship would not change their role as parents.“Most importantly, we’ll always be a family and continue showing up together for our daughter, so you’ll still see us all together from time to time. We’re at peace with this decision and just ask that our privacy is respected as we navigate this new chapter.”Baptiste also shared a similar message about the breakup, according to Hindustan Times. articles.title: Eleições 2026: conheça a cidade de SP com a votação percentual mais expressiva para Flávio Bolsonaro | G1
articles.standfirst: Desempenho em Saltinho superou o percentual obtido por Jair Bolsonaro no município em 2022. Com 4.465 votos, candidato do PL recebeu quase oito em cada dez votos válidos.
articles.summary: Desempenho em Saltinho superou o percentual obtido por Jair Bolsonaro no município em 2022. Com 4.465 votos, candidato do PL recebeu quase oito em cada dez votos válidos.
articles.body:
Flávio Bolsonaro e Lula — Foto: Evaristo Sá/AFP e Amanda Perobelli/Reuters

Com pouco mais de 8 mil habitantes e localizada na Região Metropolitana de Piracicaba, Saltinho (SP) foi a cidade onde Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) obteve o desempenho percentual mais expressivo no estado de São Paulo.

O candidato recebeu 78,71% dos votos válidos , o que representou a escolha de 4.465 dos 5.860 eleitores que compareceram às urnas neste domingo (4).

Já o atual presidente Lula (PT) recebeu 15,25% da preferência, o que totalizou 865 votos.

O resultado percentual de Flávio Bolsonaro no 1º turno foi maior que o obtido pelo pai em 2022 .

Na ocasião, Jair Bolsonaro (PL) teve 75,77% dos votos para a Presidência (4.143 votos), enquanto Lula foi a escolha de 16,62% dos eleitores (909 votos) do município.

Localizado a cerca de 180 km da capital paulista, Saltinho tem origem ligada à expansão agrícola da região de Piracicaba e forte influência da imigração italiana.

O município nasceu como distrito de Piracicaba (SP) em 1922, passou por mudanças administrativas ao longo do século passado e conquistou a emancipação político-administrativa em 1991, após aprovação em plebiscito.

Informações da página oficial da Câmara Municipal explicam que o nome da cidade surgiu por causa de uma pequena queda d´água no Córrego do Saltinho , logo após a sua cabeceira.

Foto de arquivo de geada na zona rural de Saltinho em 30 de julho de 2021 — Foto: Luís Carlos Alves Pereira/Arquivo pessoal

A abstenção no 1º turno das eleições de 2026, neste domingo (4), em Piracicaba (SP) e em mais seis cidades da região ultrapassou o índice do país, que foi de 21,08% .

Dos 958.295 eleitores aptos a votar nas 18 cidades da área de cobertura do g1 Piracicaba , 195.663 deixaram de ir às urnas. A taxa de abstenção da região foi de 20,41%.

O maior índice entre as cidades foi a de São Pedro (SP), com 25,36%. Já o menor foi em Rafard (SP), com 16,63%.

Além de Piracicaba e São Pedro, Águas de São Pedro (SP), Charqueada (SP), Cosmópolis (SP), Engenheiro Coelho (SP) e Ipeúna (SP) superaram a abstenção nacional.

Maiores cidades da região, Piracicaba e Limeira (SP) foram na contramão no comparativo com o primeiro turno das eleições de 2022, quando registraram 22,05% e 20,74%, respectivamente . Enquanto a primeira viu as faltas subirem neste ano, a segunda registrou queda.

articles.title: As cidades de São Paulo onde Flávio Bolsonaro venceu e onde Lula ficou na frente | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidato do PL foi o mais votado na maioria dos municípios paulistas; petista ganhou em 39 cidades, incluindo a capital, segundo levantamento com 100% das urnas.
articles.summary: Candidato do PL foi o mais votado na maioria dos municípios paulistas; petista ganhou em 39 cidades, incluindo a capital, segundo levantamento com 100% das urnas.
articles.body:
Flávio Bolsonaro e Lula — Foto: Evaristo Sá/AFP e Amanda Perobelli/Reuters

Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) venceu em 605 cidades de São Paulo no primeiro turno da eleição presidencial de 2026, enquanto Lula (PT) ficou na frente em 39 municípios, segundo o levantamento de apuração com 100% das urnas. A capital paulista foi uma das cidades em que o presidente venceu.

O resultado mostra uma vantagem de Flávio no interior e em grande parte da região metropolitana. Lula, por sua vez, concentrou suas vitórias principalmente em municípios da Grande São Paulo e em algumas cidades do interior e do Vale do Ribeira.

Flávio ficou na frente nas demais cidades listadas no levantamento, incluindo grandes municípios como Campinas, Guarulhos, Osasco, Santos, São José dos Campos, Sorocaba, Ribeirão Preto, São José do Rio Preto, Bauru, Piracicaba, Jundiaí, Mogi das Cruzes e Santo André.

Entre as cidades em que o candidato do PL venceu também estão municípios do litoral, como Santos, Guarujá, Praia Grande, São Vicente, Caraguatatuba, Ubatuba e Ilhabela, além de cidades do interior e da região metropolitana.

Na cidade de São Paulo, Lula venceu Flávio Bolsonaro por uma diferença de pouco mais de quatro pontos percentuais: 46,58% a 42,13%. Foram cerca de 3 milhões de votos para o presidente e 2,7 milhões para o candidato do PL.

O resultado também se refletiu nas zonas eleitorais: Lula venceu em 35 zonas, enquanto Flávio ficou na frente em 22.

A cidade onde Flávio Bolsonaro alcançou seu maior percentual foi Saltinho, com 78,71% dos votos. Lula teve seu melhor desempenho proporcional em Itapura, com 62,57%.

articles.body:
Flávio Bolsonaro e Javier Milei em foto posada. — Foto: Reprodução / Redes Sociais

O presidente da Argentina, Javier Milei, parabenizou neste domingo (4) o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) pelo desempenho no primeiro turno das eleições presidenciais brasileiras. Em publicação nas redes sociais, Milei classificou o resultado como uma "eleição histórica" e afirmou esperar trabalhar com o candidato caso ele seja eleito presidente.

"A liberdade avança no Brasil . Parabéns, querido amigo Flávio Bolsonaro, por esta eleição histórica contra o comunista Lula", escreveu o presidente argentino.

Na mensagem, Milei também afirmou que o continente americano pertence aos cidadãos que querem viver em liberdade e defendeu a aproximação entre Brasil e Argentina.

"Espero que em breve possamos começar a trabalhar juntos para que a Argentina e o Brasil continuem sendo grandes parceiros comerciais, culturais e políticos. As oportunidades para nossas nações, trabalhando juntos, são infinitas", declarou.

A manifestação ocorreu após a confirmação de que Flávio Bolsonaro e o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) disputarão o segundo turno das eleições presidenciais , marcado para 25 de outubro.

Segundo dados do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE), com 99,99% das urnas apuradas, Flávio tinha 47,03% dos votos válidos, à frente de Lula, que somava 45,16%.

Daqui a três semanas, os eleitores voltarão às urnas para decidir quem comandará o país pelos próximos quatro anos. Se eleito, Flávio Bolsonaro assumirá a Presidência aos 45 anos. Caso vença a disputa do dia 25 de outubro, Lula iniciará seu quarto mandato presidencial aos 81 anos.

A eleição de 2026 consolidou novamente a polarização entre bolsonarismo e petismo. Flávio e Lula avançaram ao segundo turno após superarem outros nove candidatos que participaram da disputa.

Milei é um aliado político da família Bolsonaro e já manifestou apoio a Jair Bolsonaro em outras ocasiões.

articles.title: Tio e sobrinha, Carlos e Luna Zarattini são eleitos deputados federais por São Paulo | G1
articles.standfirst: Carlos Zarattini (PT) teve 117.596 votos, enquanto Luna Zarattini (PT) recebeu 233.733 votos; os dois representam gerações diferentes de uma família com trajetória política ligada ao PT e à esquerda.
articles.summary: Carlos Zarattini (PT) teve 117.596 votos, enquanto Luna Zarattini (PT) recebeu 233.733 votos; os dois representam gerações diferentes de uma família com trajetória política ligada ao PT e à esquerda.
articles.body:
Carlos Zarattini (PT), de 67 anos, e sua sobrinha Luna Zarattini (PT), de 32 anos, foram eleitos deputados federais por São Paulo neste domingo (4). — Foto: Reprodução

São Paulo elegeu dois integrantes da família Zarattini para a Câmara dos Deputados nas eleições deste domingo (4): Carlos Zarattini (PT), de 67 anos, e sua sobrinha Luna Zarattini (PT), de 32 anos.

Carlos recebeu 117.596 votos e Luna teve 233.733 votos. Com o resultado, tio e sobrinha passam a integrar a bancada paulista na Câmara.

A eleição de Luna representa também a continuidade de uma trajetória política familiar iniciada antes mesmo da criação do PT. Ela é neta de Ricardo Zarattini, uma das referências históricas da família e militante da esquerda que foi perseguido e preso durante a ditadura militar.

Luna já havia seguido os passos do avô e do tio na política ao se eleger vereadora de São Paulo em 2024.

A história política dos Zarattini tem como principal personagem da geração anterior Ricardo Zarattini, avô de Luna e pai de Carlos. Militante de esquerda durante a ditadura militar, Ricardo foi preso político e, em 1969, esteve entre os presos libertados em troca do embaixador dos Estados Unidos no Brasil, Charles Elbrick.

A trajetória da família se aproximou do PT desde a formação do partido. Carlos Zarattini construiu sua carreira política pela legenda e chegou à Câmara dos Deputados pela primeira vez em 2006. Desde então, foi reeleito sucessivamente e, com o resultado de 2026, conquistou um novo mandato.

Antes de chegar à Câmara, Carlos também foi deputado estadual em São Paulo. Na eleição de 2022, havia sido reeleito deputado federal com 147.349 votos.

Luna é da geração seguinte. Ela é filha da repórter-fotográfica Mônica Zarattini e sobrinha de Carlos. A trajetória política começou ainda na juventude, quando se envolveu com movimentos estudantis e, posteriormente, com pautas ligadas à educação e às desigualdades sociais.

Em 2020, Luna tentou pela primeira vez uma vaga na Câmara Municipal de São Paulo, mas não foi eleita. Em 2023, assumiu como suplente e, no ano seguinte, foi eleita vereadora pelo PT com cerca de 100 mil votos.

Na Câmara Municipal, tornou-se líder da bancada petista e presidiu a Comissão de Direitos Humanos.

Ao falar sobre sua trajetória política, Luna já apontou o avô como uma de suas principais referências. Ricardo Zarattini é descrito por ela como uma inspiração política, especialmente pela atuação durante a ditadura militar e pela ligação com as lutas da esquerda.

A chegada de Luna à Câmara dos Deputados, portanto, coloca três gerações da família Zarattini na trajetória política brasileira: Ricardo, Carlos e agora Luna, embora em períodos diferentes.

Carlos, que iniciou sua carreira política ainda durante a ditadura e posteriormente se tornou uma das figuras tradicionais do PT paulista, agora dividirá a bancada federal com a sobrinha, que chega ao Congresso aos 32 anos.

Nas eleições deste ano, Luna foi uma das candidatas mais votadas para deputado federal em São Paulo, com 233.733 votos, ficando entre os dez primeiros colocados no estado. Carlos, com 117.596 votos, também garantiu uma das 70 cadeiras destinadas a São Paulo na Câmara.

articles.title: This 1906 Australian house was saved from demolition; the former Chinese-Australian family home is now becoming a museum
articles.summary: Ballarat councillors have voted unanimously to seek interim heritage protection for Victory House, a home built in 1906 at 742 Geelong Road in the suburb
articles.body: Ballarat councillors have voted unanimously to seek interim heritage protection for Victory House, a home built in 1906 at 742 Geelong Road in the suburb of Canadian. Named after the 1902 Melbourne Cup winner The Victory, it was home to the family of Chinese goldmine manager James Wong Chung until 2008. Landowners want to demolish the house and outbuildings for four dwellings, but the interim protection will prevent that while permanent controls are sought. Chinese Australian Cultural Society Ballarat president Charles Zhang says the long-term goal is to buy the site and turn it into a museum and cultural centre.Why was the 1906 Australian house called Victory HouseAs reported by ABC News, Victory House was built in 1906 and named after the 1902 Melbourne Cup winner The Victory. It was home to the family of Chinese goldmine manager James Wong Chung. According to family history and the council, the family put winnings from that race toward building the Edwardian dwelling. The name "Victory" is etched in the fanlight above the front door. The citation records the Chung family's association with the property for more than 100 years, until 2008.James Wong Chung also worked as an interpreter for the government, assisting with legal and other matters for members of the Ballarat Chinese community. It states that family members held leadership roles in the textile and railways unions. According to the report, the house was remembered by family members as a welcoming place where Chinese heritage and culture were celebrated through informal visits and annual gatherings of up to 200 people of Chinese background.Why was the 1906 Australian house considered locally significantA City of Ballarat officers' report to the Planning Delegated Committee says a history report dated 21 June 2022, prepared by Dr Robyn Ballinger of History Making Pty Ltd, found the dwelling meets the threshold of local significance. The Statement of Significance describes the place as being of local historical, social and associative significance to the City of Ballarat. It lists the contributing elements as the c.1906 dwelling with c.1925 alterations, the mature Cypress hedges, the former miner's residence (c.1880) to the north of the dwelling, and the decorative carved fireplaces and surrounds. The assessment cites Criteria A, H and G.The report also sets out other processes affecting the site. A request under Section 29A of the Building Act 1993 to demolish the dwelling and outbuildings was received on 7 July 2022. The report states that this request has been suspended. It notes that Heritage Victoria found an Interim Protection Order was not warranted but listed the property on the Victorian Heritage Inventory for its archaeological significance. On 26 August 2022, the Heritage Council of Victoria approved an Interim Protection Order under the Heritage Act 2017 while it reviews the place for State-level significance.Why do the landowners want to demolish the historic Australian houseChinese Australian Cultural Society Ballarat president Charles Zhang says the long-term goal is to purchase the site and turn it into a museum and cultural centre. “We are saving this house because we want to save this history," Zhang told ABC. He said the money was there, thanks to private donors. Mick Trembath, whose family has lived in the house across six generations, supports the plan to approach the owner about purchasing the property. He said he was surprised and overjoyed at the council's vote.The landowners want to demolish the house and outbuildings to construct four new dwellings, and the interim protection will prevent that while permanent protections are sought. Councillor Mark Harris, who was one of the four who originally voted against protection, told ABC Ballarat that he had not changed his mind on the heritage value of the home itself. articles.summary: On her sixth birthday in 1932, Princess Elizabeth, who would later become Queen Elizabeth the Second, received a present that most children could only
articles.body: On her sixth birthday in 1932, Princess Elizabeth, who would later become Queen Elizabeth the Second, received a present that most children could only dream about, a small house of her very own. Named Y Bwthyn Bach, which means the Little Cottage, it stood in the grounds of Royal Lodge in Windsor Great Park, the country home her parents took over when she was six. The gift came from the people of Wales. It offers a charming glimpse of a quieter royal childhood, before the events of 1936 changed everything for her family.Princess Elizabeth's sixth birthday gift and her own small houseAccording to the official royal website, Princess Elizabeth was given her own small house in the grounds of Royal Lodge, the country home in Windsor Great Park that her parents had taken over when she was six years old. Its name, Y Bwthyn Bach, is Welsh for the Little Cottage. The website describes it as a gift from the people of Wales, presented for her sixth birthday in 1932. For a young princess whom her family did not expect to become monarch, it was a remarkable present. The website offers no further description of the building, so details such as its rooms and furnishings are not recorded there.How a small house came to stand in the grounds of Royal LodgePrincess Elizabeth was born on 21 April 1926 at 17 Bruton Street in Mayfair, London, the home of her maternal grandparents, the Earl and Countess of Strathmore. She was the first child of the Duke and Duchess of York, who later became King George VI and Queen Elizabeth. When she was six years old, her parents took over Royal Lodge in Windsor Great Park as their own country home. In its grounds stood Y Bwthyn Bach, the Little Cottage, a gift from the people of Wales for her sixth birthday in 1932. The young princess therefore had a small house of her own within the family's countryside retreat.Royal Lodge, Windsor Great Park and the family homesThe princess's earliest years were spent at 145 Piccadilly, the London house her parents took shortly after her birth, and at White Lodge in Richmond Park. She also spent time at the homes of her paternal grandparents, King George V and Queen Mary, including Windsor Castle, Balmoral Castle and Sandringham House. Her mother's parents, the Earl and Countess of Strathmore, had homes she visited too, including Glamis Castle in Angus, Scotland, and Saint Paul's Walden Bury in Hertfordshire. In 1930, her sister, Princess Margaret Rose, was born, and the royal website describes the family of four as very close. Royal Lodge later became their own country home.From a quiet childhood to the abdication of 1936When Princess Elizabeth was born, she and her family did not expect that she would one day become monarch. Her quiet family life came to an end in 1936, when her grandfather, King George V, died and his eldest son came to the throne as King Edward the Eighth. Before the end of the year, he decided to give up the throne in order to marry Wallis Simpson. In December, her father became King George VI, and she became first in line to the throne. articles.title: Her father died in a plane crash in 2007; 19 years later, daughter is suing her mother over a $15 million farm
articles.summary: Sapphire Britt Halliday's father, mining executive Garnet Halliday, died in a plane crash in Malawi in 2007, aged 50.
articles.body: Sapphire Britt Halliday's father, mining executive Garnet Halliday, died in a plane crash in Malawi in 2007, aged 50. Nearly two decades later, Sapphire is suing her mother, Deborah Lakshmi Halliday, in the Supreme Court of Victoria over the family's farm in Macedon, Victoria, which is now worth an estimated $14 million to $15 million. Sapphire claims her mother promised her an interest in the property and the family's Waterford Charolais cattle business if she did not challenge her father's will. Deborah denies making the promise and argues that some parts of the alleged arrangement would be legally non-binding regardless. An interim court ruling has allowed the farm's sale to proceed while requiring $2.5 million to be secured for Sapphire's claim and debts against the property.Garnet Halliday died in a 2007 plane crashGarnet Halliday was a senior executive at Western Australian mining company Paladin when he died in a plane crash in Malawi in March 2007. He was 50. Halliday left behind an estate worth more than $30 million, according to ABC's reporting on the current court case. Its major assets included the Macedon farm and the Waterford Charolais cattle business, which were valued at about $3 million at the time of his death. The estate also included approximately $26 million in Paladin shares and a $1.6 million life insurance policy. Together, those reported assets amounted to about $30.6 million.That figure refers to the value of Halliday's overall estate in 2007, not the present-day value of the farm. The farm is now separately estimated to be worth between $14 million and $15 million. Halliday's will left $50,000 to Kaden, his son from a previous marriage, with the remainder of the estate going to his wife, Deborah. Kaden subsequently challenged the will and received a further payout. Sapphire was 18 at the time.Sapphire says her mother promised her a share of the farmSapphire's case centres on what she says her mother promised after Halliday's death. According to her claim, Deborah told her that if she did not challenge her father's will, she would eventually receive an interest in the farm worth about $2 million. Sapphire says she understood that amount to be comparable to the payout her half-brother received after challenging the will. She also claims she was promised a 50 per cent share in the cattle business.The court also heard Sapphire's allegation that Deborah promised to leave her own share of the farm to her daughter in her will, provided the property was not sold and Sapphire continued helping to run the family business. Deborah denies making the alleged promise and argues that parts of the arrangement would not be legally binding even if such assurances had been given. Sapphire told the court that she relied on her mother's assurances by giving up her right to challenge the will and abandoning plans to study agriculture at university. She later worked on the farm for more than a decade, which she claims was for below-award wages. These remain allegations made in the proceedings and have not been finally determined.Text messages became part of Sapphire's caseText messages exchanged between the mother and daughter in May 2023 were tendered to the court. In one message, Deborah told Sapphire: "I hoped to pay you out like I paid [Mr Halliday's son]," but added that she could not afford to do so at the time. Sapphire's court documents also allege that Deborah told her on another occasion that "the farm is mine." Sapphire lodged a caveat over the farm on July 1, 2025, claiming an interest in the property on the basis of proprietary estoppel. In broad terms, her case argues that she relied on her mother's alleged assurances and that it would be unfair for Deborah to go back on them.Deborah told the court she did not know Sapphire was making a claim over the property until she received a solicitor's letter three days after the caveat was lodged. The dispute has unfolded as Deborah attempts to sell the farm. The court heard that she suffered a stroke in 2021, which made it more difficult to operate a business that had already been trading at a loss for several years. Since late 2023, she had borrowed close to $1 million against the property from several parties, including a private couple, a litigation funder covering her legal costs and another lender providing cash flow assistance. Her total debt was put at about $2.5 million, while two lenders had also lodged caveats over the property.Court allows the farm sale while protecting the claimThe immediate issue before Associate Justice Barrett was whether Sapphire's caveat should remain over the property while her underlying claim continued. The ruling did not determine whether Deborah had actually made the promises Sapphire alleges or whether Sapphire is ultimately entitled to the farm or its proceeds. Barrett found that Sapphire had established a prima facie case for proprietary estoppel. However, the judge found that a claim to two-thirds of the farm's value was stronger than her claim to the whole property without any debt. The judge also considered the wording of the text messages relied upon by Sapphire. The messages referred to a payment of between $1.5 million and $2 million, or to a percentage of the farm's sale price, rather than clearly establishing a claim to the entire property.The court then weighed the potential impact on Deborah's creditors against the risk to Sapphire if the property were sold without protecting her claim. Barrett allowed the sale to proceed but ordered that Sapphire's caveat be removed on the condition that $2.5 million be paid into court or an agreed trust account. The money is intended to protect Sapphire's claim as well as debts secured against the property since she lodged her caveat, while the underlying dispute continues. The ruling is therefore not a final decision on the inheritance dispute. No trial date had been set when ABC reported the case on September 23, 2026, and the matter is scheduled for mediation in March 2027.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Elon Musk admits that Tesla Robotaxis have a 'cat problem'; and one which Google’s Waymo does not ‘agree’ with
articles.summary: Elon Musk has acknowledged that Tesla’s Robotaxi service is struggling to operate late into the night because its vehicles have trouble spotting small
articles.body: Elon Musk has acknowledged that Tesla’s Robotaxi service is struggling to operate late into the night because its vehicles have trouble spotting small animals in the dark -- a challenge highlighting long-standing criticisms of the company’s camera-only autonomous driving system. Addressing why the service has been slow to expand after dark, Tesla CEO pointed to low-light, low-contrast detection as the key obstacle, specifically citing the difficulty of identifying "grey kittens on grey tarmac."The remarks came after Tesla announced recently that its Austin Robotaxi pilot would extend operating hours by another one hour, moving its night time up from 10:00 PM to 11:00 PM. Despite the incremental gain, the service remains more constrained than when it debuted in June 2025 with operating hours spanning 6:00 AM to midnight. Musk quoted a post from Robotaxi handle on X, formerly Twitter that announced Robotaxi being now available till 11 pm, Musk wrote, "Robotaxi operating hours moved from 10pm to 11pm. The main thing we’re trying to solve is making sure that we don’t run over pets when they’re hard to see at night. Literally trying to avoid grey kittens on grey tarmac in the dark."Elon Musk on Tesla's 'kitten problem'The technical bottleneck Elon Musk described exposes a classic limitation of optical cameras. As passive sensors, cameras depend entirely on ambient illumination and contrast to distinguish objects from their background. A low-contrast subject, such as a grey animal against dark asphalt, reflects minimal light and provides little distinct visual data.By contrast, active sensors like lidar and radar do not rely on ambient lighting. Lidar projects its own laser pulses to generate precise, real-time 3D depth maps, detecting any object that protrudes above the road surface regardless of colour or darkness. Radar emits radio waves to track distance and velocity, cutting through fog, dust, and glare that routinely blind camera lenses.Commercial autonomous fleets operating at scale -- like Google-parent Alphabet’s Waymo -- rely on a multi-sensor suite combining cameras, lidar, and radar to run 24-hour operations across thousands of vehicles. Also in contrast to Robotaxis, Waymo's driverless vehicles run 24 hours a day.How Google’s Waymo has solved ‘kitten problem’In August this year, Waymo co-CEO Dmitri Dolgov demonstrated this capability by releasing footage of children and dogs running across an unlit street; while the optical cameras struggled with visibility, the lidar feed tracked the subjects clearly. Dolgov made the comments during a talk at Y Combinator’s Startup School as he walked the audience through the lessons Waymo has learned building its driver over close to two decades.Tesla, however, has pursued a strictly vision-only strategy under Musk’s direction. Musk has spent years dismissing competing hardware setups, famously calling lidar a “fool’s errand” in 2019 and later claiming that combining sensors causes conflicting data that reduces overall safety. Tesla stripped radar units from its production vehicles in 2021, phased out ultrasonic sensors in 2022, and has consistently avoided lidar, even saying that anyone relying on it is "doomed."Incidentally, safety regulators are scrutinising the company’s approach. The US National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) is actively investigating 3.2 million Tesla vehicles over FSD collisions in low-visibility environments. As part of that inquiry, federal investigators requested internal company communications, including a document titled "Radar Saves Us", recalling Musk’s private admission in 2021 that vision paired with high-resolution radar would outperform vision alone.You use AI every day. articles.title: Flydubai co-pilot likely acted alone; Israeli probe finds no terror link for now - report
articles.summary: New reports suggest that the Omani co-pilot accused of attacking the captain and trying to seize control of a Flydubai flight bound for Tel Aviv probably
articles.body: New reports suggest that the Omani co-pilot accused of attacking the captain and trying to seize control of a Flydubai flight bound for Tel Aviv probably acted alone.An Israeli official told CNN that information gathered during the investigation so far suggested Hamam al-Hammami acted alone. Another Israeli source said Israel had found no known link between the suspect and any group or government, while stressing that the investigation was still ongoing.The development comes as investigators examine whether al-Hammami made a further attempt to bring down the Boeing 737 after his initial attack on Captain Smit Machchhar failed. An investigation by Italian newspaper Corriere della Sera, cited by Ynet News, said investigators were examining whether the co-pilot moved the aircraft's two engine fuel switches from “Run” to “Cutoff” after taking control of the plane.According to the report, al-Hammami allegedly pushed the aircraft into a steep descent after disabling the autopilot, potentially attempting to crash it in the Saudi desert after passengers and crew began thwarting his attempt to seize the aircraft.What happened inside the cockpitThe incident took place on September 30 aboard Flydubai flight FZ1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv.Al-Hammami allegedly attacked Machchhar with a cockpit crash axe and attempted to take control of the aircraft. Despite being wounded, Machchhar managed to activate the mechanism that opened the cockpit door, allowing cabin crew and passengers to enter and help subdue the co-pilot. The aircraft eventually made an emergency landing in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia.The UAE attorney general has described the incident as an attempted “terrorist act”. Investigations are being conducted by authorities in the UAE, Israel and Saudi Arabia.US president Donald Trump had earlier suggested that al-Hammami could be linked to Iran, saying it was “based on what I’m hearing”. He did not provide details. Israeli sources now say they have not identified a link to any group or government, although the investigation has not concluded.Questions over his pastAl-Hammami, 29, is an Omani national who had previously worked for Oman Air. According to CNN, he was removed from his previous job after concerns about his extremist views. He later joined Flydubai and had been working there for around eight months.Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu has separately said al-Hammami had undergone “Islamist radical indoctrination”, based on information gathered during questioning. He did not provide further details.The investigation has also raised questions over aviation security and the vetting of foreign flight crews.CNN reported that the names of all passengers and crew had been provided to Israeli authorities before the flight took off. Israel's tax authority confirmed receiving the list, but the transportation ministry said its protocols did not include checking the names of flight crew members.The issue is particularly sensitive because Oman does not have formal diplomatic relations with Israel. Netanyahu has said Israel had longstanding arrangements aimed at preventing pilots from countries without diplomatic ties from flying into the country and described the case as exposing a “loophole”.Israel has since ordered a review of security procedures for foreign civil aviation following the incident.You use AI every day. articles.title: They built a grocery store in Wisconsin in 1987; decades later, the couple protected nearly 14 acres for their great-grandchildren to inherit
articles.summary: In Ellison Bay, Wisconsin, nearly 14 acres of prairie, forest and ridge and swale wetlands are now protected through a conservation easement with the Door
articles.body: In Ellison Bay, Wisconsin, nearly 14 acres of prairie, forest and ridge and swale wetlands are now protected through a conservation easement with the Door County Land Trust. The land belongs to Vonnie and Dave Callsen, who founded Main Street Market in Egg Harbour and have been staples in Door County since opening it in 1987. According to the Door County Land Trust, the land also protects groundwater resources contributing to the Mink River Estuary and Hine's emerald dragonfly habitat. The couple have six great-grandchildren, and Vonnie Callsen said they want them to have the same beauty that she and Dave enjoy.How did the couple build their Wisconsin grocery store in 1987Vonnie and Dave Callsen are the founders of the "iconic grocery store, Main Street Market in Egg Harbour". The story states that the couple have been staples in Door County since they opened the store in 1987. They had owned their property for longer than that, and they officially became residents in the same year.The Door County Land Trust reports that when the couple first bought the property, there was no house, only an old barn, an apple orchard and nearly 30 acres of natural beauty. They camped on the land and put a kitchen and a bathroom into the barn before building their house a few years later. According to the story, Dave Callsen previously served on the DCLT board as Board President, and both he and Vonnie are Legacy Circle members.Why did the couple preserve nearly 14 acres in Ellison BayThe couple wished to preserve a piece of their land to protect a prairie and forest with thriving wildlife, and an area of ridge and swale wetlands. According to the organisation, the land also protects groundwater resources that contribute to the Mink River Estuary, as well as Hine's emerald dragonfly habitat.The story quotes Dave Callsen on what the land means to him: "I don't think there's anything like getting up in the morning and looking outside to see what nature has brought today." The Callsens' easement covers nearly 14 acres in Ellison Bay.How does the Callsens’ land buffer existing protected landsAccording to Drew Reinke, the Door County Land Trust's Senior Conservation Easement Manager, "One of the most impressive aspects of completing the Callsen Family conservation easement is that it buffers existing protected lands—specifically, The Nature Conservancy's Mink River Preserve." He noted that DCLT conservation easements on properties abutting protected lands are becoming increasingly common across the peninsula.The Door County Land Trust also reports that the property is near the Clearing Folk School, a 120-acre conservation easement protected since 2006. The story states that when the organisation assesses land to protect, lands bordering existing protected properties, or particularly vulnerable habitats, are the highest priority. This made the Callsens' land a perfect candidate for a conservation easement.How does a conservation easement protect landA conservation easement is a voluntary legal agreement between a property owner and a land trust or other qualified organisation. The agreement permanently protects the property's identified conservation values by restricting certain uses and activities that could compromise those values. It does not require an owner to vacate or sell the land. Owners retain ownership and can continue to use and enjoy the property, and they can pass it on to their heirs or sell it to a future owner, who will likewise be bound by the easement. Dave Callsen is quoted as saying: "You're not giving your property away. You still have it, you can use it, you can live on it."Vonnie Callsen said: "We have six great-grandchildren, and we want them to have the same beauty that we have. That's why we're trying to save as much as we can." Dave Callsen added: "The beauty of the land is only there because people will it to be there." Private landowners such as the Callsens play a vital role in preserving Door County's natural character at a time when land prices have skyrocketed, and conservation funding is plummeting. Vonnie Callsen also said: "We need to get more young people involved."You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: In 2007, black rats were eradicated from Italy’s Zannone island; by 2016, Scopoli’s shearwater breeding pairs had risen from 27 to 80
articles.summary: On a Mediterranean island off Italy, a conservation project aimed at removing an invasive rodent produced a change that could be seen in the seabird
articles.body: On a Mediterranean island off Italy, a conservation project aimed at removing an invasive rodent produced a change that could be seen in the seabird colony. Zannone had been among the larger Italian islands targeted in the country’s expanding rat eradication programme. The work was part of a wider effort to remove black rats from islands where they posed a threat to native wildlife, particularly seabirds that nest in burrows. On Zannone, the eradication was completed in 2007. The number of breeding pairs of Scopoli’s shearwater subsequently rose from 27 in 2007 to 80 in 2016, giving conservationists a clear example of how removing an introduced predator could alter the fortunes of an island bird colony.Black rat eradication transforms Italy’s islands for native wildlifeBlack rats, or Rattus rattus, have been removed from a growing number of Italian islands since the late 1990s. The work was supported in many cases by the European Union’s LIFE programme, which helped fund projects designed to protect native island ecosystems. By the time of the review, rats had been eradicated from 14 Italian islands, with projects under way on five others.Islands offered a particular advantage for this kind of intervention. Their isolation can make eradication more manageable than it would be on a mainland landscape, while also helping to protect the result once the invasive animals have been removed. The projects varied considerably, however. Some islands were tiny, while others covered hundreds or thousands of hectares. Some were uninhabited, while others contained homes and small communities. Terrain was another consideration, with steep or inaccessible areas making conventional bait placement difficult.Zannone tests new methods for black rat eradicationZannone was larger and more difficult to treat than the very small islands where some of Italy’s earliest eradication projects had taken place. According to the Occasional Paper of the IUCN Species Survival Commission titled ‘Black rat eradication on Italian islands: planning forward by looking backward’ rats had begun to be eradicated from islands exceeding 100 hectares from 2005 onwards, with Zannone among them.The island’s uneven terrain also influenced how bait was distributed. On Zannone, bait stations were used at a lower density than during some earlier operations. In areas that could not easily be reached, rodenticide bait blocks were hand-broadcast from a helicopter. The blocks were placed inside biodegradable bamboo dispensers before being distributed.As conservation teams gained experience, techniques were adapted to the physical conditions of individual islands rather than relying on one standard method. Larger islands presented different logistical problems from small, relatively accessible sites, while the presence of other animals also had to be considered when selecting bait and delivery methods.What makes black rats a threat to burrowing seabirdsScopoli’s shearwaters are burrow-nesting seabirds, and rats can be particularly damaging to species that breed in this way. The Italian review points to evidence from several Mediterranean islands where declines in burrowing seabirds had been associated mainly with introduced predators, especially rats. The species affected included Scopoli’s shearwater, Yelkouan shearwater, Balearic shearwater and European storm petrel.The difference was also visible in breeding success. When data for Scopoli’s and Yelkouan shearwaters were pooled, islands without rats recorded a considerably higher breeding success than islands where rats remained. The figures given in the review were 0.78 on islands without rats compared with 0.14 on islands with rats.Rat-free islands saw Scopoli’s shearwater colonies growThe Zannone figures are among the clearest in the review. After the rat eradication in 2007, the Scopoli’s shearwater colony increased from 27 breeding pairs in 2007 to 80 pairs in 2016.In simple numerical terms, that was an increase of 53 pairs. The colony was therefore nearly three times its earlier size by 2016. The source presents the figures as an example of the effect rat removal had on shearwater colonies, rather than as an isolated population count detached from the wider eradication programme.Zannone was not the only island where a colony expanded following rat removal. At La Scola, the review records a rise in the Scopoli’s shearwater colony from between 60 and 100 pairs in 2001 to between 150 and 250 pairs in 2010, ten years after eradication, as reported. These examples helped illustrate why shearwater populations were considered when Italian conservationists decided which islands should receive priority.Conservationists turned to biosecurity after removing island ratsEradication did not mean the conservation work could simply stop. Rats can return to islands, either by swimming from nearby land or islands or through human transport. The review records reinvasions on several Italian islands and notes that some occurred where neighbouring rat populations remained.The distances involved could be surprisingly small. In the cases examined, reinvading rats had travelled from nearby islands or the mainland, with the maximum distance recorded at 320 metres and the average at about 219 metres. That made biosecurity an important part of maintaining an island after an eradication project had been completed.The researchers also describe how better understanding of rat movements and quarantine practices made it possible to attempt projects in places where reinvasion had previously been considered too risky. Monitoring boats, ports and other possible routes of entry became part of the wider effort to keep islands rat-free.More than 1,500 hectares of Italian islands were cleared of ratsBy the time of the review, completed projects had left more than 1,500 hectares of Italian islands free of rats, while ongoing or planned work was expected to increase that area substantially. About 15% of the Italian population of shearwater pairs covered by the assessment had been released from rat predation.The Zannone result therefore sits within a much larger conservation programme. The island itself provided a relatively contained setting in which removing an invasive predator could be followed by changes in a native seabird colony. Changes to European biocide rules made some later eradication projects harder to carry out, particularly where aerial bait distribution was required. Italian authorities interpreted the regulations in ways that restricted how rodenticides could be distributed, leading to disputes and delays on some islands.You use AI every day. articles.title: October 2026 Feng Shui: Why a Mirror Opposite Your Main Door Could Matter Before You Reset Your Home
articles.summary: Walk through your front door and look straight ahead. Is there a mirror staring back at you? It's one of the most common setups in American homes.
articles.body: Walk through your front door and look straight ahead. Is there a mirror staring back at you?It's one of the most common setups in American homes. A mirror in the entryway feels practical. You check your hair, grab your keys and head out. But in feng shui, that exact spot is one of the most debated placements in the house.And with fall cleaning season in full swing, October is a good time to rethink it.Why the Front Door Matters So MuchFeng shui treats the main door as the "mouth of chi." It's the entry point for energy, opportunities and, in many traditions, money.So whatever greets that energy first shapes how it moves through the rest of your home. A cluttered hallway slows it down. A bright, open entry invites it in.The Problem With a Mirror Facing the DoorMirrors reflect. That's their whole job. Many feng shui practitioners believe a mirror placed directly opposite the front door pushes incoming energy right back outside before it ever settles.Think of it like opening the door for a guest and then immediately showing them out. Nothing gets a chance to stay.People who follow this idea often link it to a feeling that money comes in and leaves just as fast. Or that new opportunities show up but never quite stick.Not every school agrees, though. Some practitioners say a mirror at the door is fine if the view behind you is pleasant. Others argue it doubles any clutter it reflects. So treat it as a guideline, not a hard rule.Where to Move It InsteadYou don't need to get rid of the mirror. Just shift it.On a side wall. A mirror on a wall perpendicular to the door still lets you check your reflection on the way out. And it guides energy deeper into the home instead of bouncing it back.In the dining room. Many practitioners love a mirror that reflects the dining table. It symbolically doubles the food and abundance in your household.Reflecting something beautiful. A window with a garden view or a nice piece of art in the mirror brings more of that good energy into the room.Placements to AvoidKeep mirrors away from the foot of your bed. Feng shui sees this as disruptive to sleep and relationships.Also skip mirrors that reflect a toilet, a messy corner or sharp edges like the corner of a cabinet. And replace any cracked or cloudy mirror. Broken glass is believed to fragment energy.What about those small octagonal bagua mirrors? Those are meant for outside the home, usually above the door, never inside facing it.The 2026 Connection2026 is the Year of the Fire Horse in the Chinese calendar. Fire energy is fast and bold, and some practitioners suggest balancing it with calm, steady entryways.Mirrors connect with the water element in feng shui. Placed well, they can cool and balance a fiery year. Placed badly, they create restlessness. So getting this one detail right fits the year's energy nicely.A Quick October Entryway ResetBefore you move anything, clear the floor. Shoes, packages and that pile of mail on the side table all block energy.Then wipe down the door itself, including the handle. Add a plant or a small bowl of seasonal fruit near the entry. Pumpkins and apples on a bench work perfectly this time of year.Once the space feels clear, decide where the mirror belongs. Most people notice the difference within a week. The house just feels more welcoming when you walk in.Get the latest astrology news and horoscope updates. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: Can CEC Gyanesh Kumar exercise EC powers alone? SC to hear plea today
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday is hearing pleas seeking the suspension of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday is hearing pleas seeking the suspension of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The pleas have raised questions on whether Gyanesh used powers that belong to the Election Commission without the approval of election commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi.A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana will hear the pleas filed by Patna resident Rakesh Kumar Singh and advocate Shailendra Mani Tripathi.The pleas come after an Indian Express report claimed that Sandhu and Joshi had formally objected at least 14 times over the past 10 months to decisions and orders on the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, which were allegedly issued without their knowledge or recommendation.What are the petitioners seeking?Singh's plea seeks Kumar's suspension until the final hearing, to protect the "multi-member character of the Election Commission." It asks that Sandhu and Joshi run the commission's business together in the meantime, with both agreeing on decisions, and that any vacancy be filled on the recommendation of a committee that includes the Chief Justice of India.Tripathi's plea seeks criminal proceedings against the CEC and other officials for failing in their official duty. It also seeks a declaration that all decisions, guidelines and software changes made under Kumar without the full commission's agreement are "unconstitutional, ultra vires and void ab initio," meaning illegal and invalid from the start.Tripathi relies on Section 18 of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners Act, 2023, which says the majority view prevails when commissioners differ. He argues that the law requires decisions to be taken together.What does the plea allege?On Form 6, the voter registration form, the plea alleges that a requirement for ancestral details and a link to the previous SIR was added through the poll panel's software without the legal amendment the election rules require. It claims the other two commissioners objected to the change.On Goa, it alleges the software lacked a feature to restore 97 eligible voters despite directions to verify them.On West Bengal, it claims more than 16.10 lakh appeals were filed in the EC's name against voters whose names were restored by judicial officers. It says the other two commissioners and the state's chief electoral officer did not know about these appeals or approve them.The Election Commission has said differing views are a normal part of discussions in any institution, and that all its orders are legally valid and follow the set procedures.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Why this Mizoram woman, who turned to farming after teaching, is being honoured by the UN: ‘What was the purpose of my education unless…’
articles.summary: When Z T Lalrithangi finished her studies, she was looking for a government job.
articles.body: When Z T Lalrithangi finished her studies, she was looking for a government job. She appeared for several competitive examinations, hoping to find a secure career. But after repeated failures, the former private-school teacher began asking herself whether a government job was really the only way to build a livelihood.“I thought a government job should not be my only focus to earn a living, as there are other ways to have a good income if a person really works hard,” Lalrithangi said, according to a PTI report.Today, the 35-year-old from Sangau in Mizoram’s Lawngtlai district is preparing to travel to Rome after being selected among the FAO 100 Women Heroes in Agrifood Systems and Rural Development, an initiative being held as part of the International Year of the Woman Farmer 2026 by United Nations. She is one of two women from India among 100 selected from more than 600 nominees across 131 countries.The recognition comes after she turned strawberry cultivation into a livelihood - beginning with about 1,000 saplings in 2024 and expanding to more than 10,000 strawberry plants spread across two hectares.The turning point According to Nagaland Post report, Lalrithangi, popularly known as Pi Mari-i, holds a postgraduate degree in Sociology from IGNOU. Before entering farming, she worked as a private-school teacher and had tried several competitive examinations in the hope of securing a government job.The turning point was not simply about finding another occupation. It was also about becoming financially independent.“Although my husband can support our family, I asked myself what the purpose of my education was unless I became self-dependent. All these thoughts motivated me to switch to farming,” she said.Her first experiment was with strawberries. In 2024, after learning about farmers successfully cultivating the crop in neighbouring Siaha district, she decided to try it herself.“We started and experimented with the plantation in 2024 in a small area after learning about successful strawberry cultivation by some farmers in Siaha district,” she said.She began with around 1,000 saplings on a farm about 5 km from Sangau. The first year brought her around Rs 1.5 lakh from the crop. That was enough to convince her that the experiment was worth expanding.“After earning about Rs 1.5 lakh in the initial year, we thought it was worth continuing and expanded the cultivation,” she said.By 2025, her earnings from strawberries had crossed Rs 10 lakh, according to the reports. She now grows more than 10,000 strawberry plants across two hectares, alongside avocado, banana and other fruits and vegetables. Part of her strawberry produce is also processed into strawberry wine for sale in local markets.She had no formal strawberry trainingThe farm did not begin with formal training or extensive institutional backing. Lalrithangi initially approached the authorities for assistance but was told that strawberries were not covered under the department’s project at the time.She decided to go ahead on her own. Government assistance was later extended to her in different forms. Without formal training in strawberry cultivation, Lalrithangi turned to the internet and other farmers for practical lessons. “I used to read and study from the internet, particularly farming technique tutorials available on YouTube,” she said.But finding the time to learn was another challenge. Lalrithangi was raising three children while building the farm. Her study sessions often happened late at night. “As a mother to three children, I have little time. So, I studied until late at night and sometimes while breastfeeding,” she said.Her husband, who works at a state-run primary school, and her parents-in-law supported her farming activities. Lalrithangi and her husband also spend weekends at the farm, while labourers are hired when required.“It is the collective support of my family that brings the farming to fruition and then the global recognition,” she said.From a small experiment to global recognitionThe FAO recognition is not Lalrithangi’s first acknowledgement. She was adjudged the best farmer from Lawngtlai district at the Mizoram Horti Fair 2026.Her international recognition comes under the FAO’s “100 Women Heroes in Agrifood Systems and Rural Development” initiative, which is being presented during the World Food Forum at FAO headquarters in Rome. The ceremony is scheduled for October 15, with the World Food Forum taking place from October 12 to 16.Lalrithangi was informed of her selection by the FAO through email on September 21 and is currently completing the mandatory travel documentation for Rome, according to the reports.For someone who once believed her next step depended on clearing a government examination, the journey has taken an unexpected turn. Her postgraduate education did not lead her into the career she had initially imagined. Instead, she used her willingness to learn, experimented with a crop unfamiliar to her and built her livelihood around it.Lalrithangi has credited her family, the state Horticulture Department and God’s guidance for the recognition.The woman who began with about 1,000 strawberry saplings is now headed to an FAO ceremony in Rome - not because she found the government job she once wanted, but because she chose to create another path for herself.You use AI every day. articles.title: All 3 of us ready to go to jail, says Ashutosh Ranka as CJP claims arrests ahead of October 10 nationwide protest
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Ashutosh Ranka, Saurav Das and Abhijeet Dipke have claimed that they could be arrested before October 10
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Ashutosh Ranka, Saurav Das and Abhijeet Dipke have claimed that they could be arrested before October 10 under the National Security Act (NSA) or other similar provisions, as protests over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls intensify.In posts on X, the three leaders said they were prepared to face arrest and vowed that any government action would not stop their campaign.Ranka said multiple sources had informed him that he, Das and Dipke could be arrested before October 10. He said they had been prepared to go to jail since June 6 and alleged that the government was resorting to violence out of fear."We are 30-year-olds fighting for a better, more accountable India. We have nothing to lose. You can arrest us, beat us, even kill us. But you cannot stop us," Ranka wrote.Das also claimed that the government was planning to arrest him, Dipke, Ranka and other CJP leaders, calling any such action "dictatorial". He said the younger generation had become aware of the issues and would not accept such measures.Das appealed to supporters to continue the campaign even if party leaders were arrested and called for a major mobilisation across the country from October 10.Dipke directly addressed Union home minister Amit Shah, writing: "Kitno ko arrest karoge Amit Shah? 10 Oct ko poora desh aa raha hai."The CJP has called for a nationwide gathering on October 10 over the SIR row.The claims came a day after a protest in Delhi during which around 110 people were detained, while about 15 police personnel were injured, according to police sources. Some women personnel were also injured after being bitten during the protest.Earlier on Sunday, the Indian Youth Congress (IYC) held a march from Raisina Road towards Jantar Mantar, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and accusing the Centre of shielding him.IYC national president Uday Bhanu Chib led the protest, with hundreds of workers raising slogans against the government amid heavy police deployment and barricading.Chib criticised the police for preventing protesters from reaching Jantar Mantar and alleged that the Centre was trying to protect Gyanesh Kumar.IYC leaders Rosh Jaiswal and Chitwan Godara also demanded Kumar's resignation, alleging a lack of accountability over the SIR exercise.The controversy intensified after a report in The Indian Express said Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised objections on at least 14 occasions over 10 months concerning electoral rolls, voter registration and the Election Commission's technology systems.The Election Commission rejected the suggestion that the objections reflected institutional dissent, saying operational queries, inputs and suggestions during the draft stage were part of its normal administrative process. The poll panel has also said that the decisions on the schedule for the SIR exercise were unanimous.(With agency inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: Apple may unveil new smart home hub, HomePod mini and Apple TV on October 13: Report
articles.summary: Apple is planning to hold an event on October 13, 2026, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman said in the latest edition of his weekly PowerOn newsletter.
articles.body: Apple is planning to hold an event on October 13, 2026, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman said in the latest edition of his weekly PowerOn newsletter. At the event, the company is expected to unveil its “long-awaited smart home hub with a screen, the new HomePod mini and an updated Apple TV,” Gurman stated. All three devices will have Siri AI at the core, he added. This will be the company’s first event after the September event where it unveiled 2026 iPhone lineup – iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, along with iPhone Duo. Apple’s October 13 event could mark a major push into smart home devices. Here’s what to expectApple’s new smart home hub could get a screenThe most notable launch is expected to be a new smart home hub with a built-in display, which could compete with devices such as Google Nest Hub and Amazon Echo Show. The device is rumoured to feature an S11 chip, which could support faster performance and Siri AI features. The screen could be used to show information such as weather updates, calendar events and music controls.A FaceTime camera is also among the expected features, potentially allowing the device to double as a video-calling hub. Apple is also reportedly developing a specialised operating system for the device focused on smart home controls.HomePod mini may get S11 chipApple is also expected to introduce an updated HomePod mini. The overall design may remain largely unchanged, while an upgraded S11 chip could improve performance and Siri responsiveness. The speaker could also get tighter integration with Apple’s smart home ecosystem and potentially new colour options.New Apple TV could focus on performanceThe third expected launch is an updated Apple TV. The device is rumoured to receive a more powerful chip, potentially the A19 or A19 Pro, which could improve gaming, streaming and multitasking. The updated Apple TV could also feature deeper Siri AI integration for voice-controlled navigation and smart home functions. Other possible additions include HDMI pass-through and a redesigned Siri Remote.All three devices are expected to have Siri AI at the core, according to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, making the October event potentially important for Apple’s wider smart home strategy.You use AI every day. articles.title: Complainant gets Rs 1.63 lakh payout after electric scooter faced defects, failed to deliver promised mileage
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: A Kerala district consumer commission has directed an electric scooter manufacturer to refund Rs 88,000 to a customer after finding
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A Kerala district consumer commission has directed an electric scooter manufacturer to refund Rs 88,000 to a customer after finding manufacturing defects in the vehicle, including poor battery performance and a defective front wheel bearing system. The commission also awarded him Rs 50,000 as compensation and Rs 25,000 as litigation costs. The order was passed on September 30, 2026.Why did the customer approach the commission?According to the commission order, Rajeshkumar R bought an electric scooter on February 21, 2022. The vehicle and its parts carried a three-year warranty and the dealer had represented that it would run 85 km after a six hour charge.The complainant alleged that the scooter initially managed only around 40 km on a charge. Even after servicing and replacement of batteries, the mileage did not improve. Batteries were changed in March and October 2023, but the vehicle eventually ran only 18 to 20 km on a full charge.He also complained of a loose front wheel bearing and problems with the charger. He alleged that the dealer could not repair the bearing and that spare parts were not available. He sought a refund of Rs 88,000, Rs 3 lakh as compensation and Rs 25,000 towards litigation costs.However, the manufacturer and dealer argued that the complaint was barred by limitation as it was filed on December 11, 2024, more than two years after the purchase. They also alleged that the mileage depended on factors including rider weight, terrain, tyre pressure, riding style, temperature and speed. They denied any manufacturing defect or deficiency in service.What did the consumer commission find?The bench of President Vinay Menon V and members Vidya A and Krishnankutty N K held that the complaint was not barred by limitation. The commission held the cause of action arose only when it became clear the defects could not be rectified, noting batteries were replaced as late as 2023.The commission also considered a joint report submitted by two experts in electrical and mechanical engineering. The report found an inherent defect in the front wheel shaft bearing system, insufficient battery voltage, poor charging retention, an oval-shaped shaft hole causing misalignment and mileage of only 16 km on a full charge.The commission noted that the manufacturer and dealer had objected to the expert report but had not produced evidence to disprove its findings.“Even though the OPs had stated a number of causes that might result in the condition suffered by the vehicle they had failed to prove by evidence that the factors laid out by them were, in fact, the reasons for the complaints suffered by the vehicle,” the bench further noted.The commission also noted that the opposite parties had not produced documents showing that they had provided effective service to the vehicle.“Thus, complainant has proved his case by cogent evidence. OPs have failed to disprove the evidence adduced by the complainant,” the commission said.The bench comprising president Vinay Menon V and members Vidya A and Krishnankutty N.K. held that the scooter suffered from a manufacturing defect. It said the defect was established through the expert evidence, while the opposite parties failed to disprove it.“Resultantly, we hold that the vehicle suffers from manufacturing defect. Since the vehicle is suffering from manufacturing defect no liability is being cast on OP2,” the commission further said.The commission directed the manufacturer to:Refund Rs 88,000 towards the cost of the scooter.Pay Rs 50,000 as compensation.Pay Rs 25,000 towards litigation costs.Make the payment within 45 days of receiving the order.Take possession of the scooter after making the payments.If the manufacturer fails to comply within 45 days, the customer will also be entitled to Rs 500 per month or part thereof as solatium from the date of the order.The commission partly allowed the complaint against the manufacturer and held that no liability was to be imposed on the authorised dealer. The order was pronounced on September 30, 2026.
